FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized by the Bitumen, Tar and 
Related Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Product Division Council. 


This standard provides a tool for evaluation of drain-down potential of a bitumen mixtureand therefore, helps in 
understanding the behavior of bitumen in situations encountered duringthe production, transportation, and placement of 
the bituminous mixture. The test methods specified in this standard are mainly applicable for Open-Graded Bitumen 
Mixtures (suchas open-graded friction course) and Gap-Graded Mixtures such as stone matrix asphalt (SMA). 


Open-graded bitumen mixes are those mixes which substantially lack fine aggregate in their gradation. Gap-graded 
bituminous mixes are those mixes which lack intermediate size aggregate in their gradation. 


The composition of the Committee, responsible for formulation of this standard is listed in Annex A. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, observed or 
calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding 
off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the 
same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 18104 : 2022 


Indian Standard 


METHODS FOR TESTING TAR AND BITUMINOUS 
MATERIALS — DETERMINATION OF DRAINDOWN 
CHARACTERISTICS OF UNCOMPACTEDBITUMEN MIXTURES 


1 SCOPE 


1.1 This standard prescribes the method for the 
determination of the amount of drain-down of 
uncompacted bitumen mixture when it is held at 
elevated temperatures. 


1.2 This standard is applicable to open-graded 
bitumen mixtures (such as open-graded friction 
course) and gap-graded mixtures such as Stone 
Matrix Asphalt (SMA). 


2 REFERENCE 


The following standards contain provisions which, 
through reference in text constitute provisions of this 
standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All the standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below. 


IS No. Title 
IS 334: Glossary of terms relating to bitumen and 
2002 tar (third revision) 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in 


IS 334 shall apply. 


4 METHOD A 
4.1 Principle 


A fresh sample of the bitumen mixture (either made in 
the laboratory or from Hot Mix Plant) is placed in a wire 
basket. The wire basket is hung in a forced draft oven 
for one hour at a pre-selected temperature. A catch plate 
of known mass is placed below the basket to collect 
material drained from the sample. The mass of the 
drained material is determined to calculate the amount 
of drain-down as a percentage of the mass of the total 
sample. 


4.2 Apparatus 

4.2.1 Forced Draft Oven — Least count 1 °C and 
capable of maintaining temperatures in the range of 
120 °C to 175 °C. 

4.2.2 Plates — To collect the drained material. 

4.2.3 Balance — Least count 0.1 g. 

4.2.4 Standard Wire Basket — The dimensions as 


shown in Fig. 1. Standard 6.3 mm sieve cloth shall be 
used to make the basket. 


Wire basket assembly 


Basket Bottom 


Top View 


165 mm 


= 
| 108 mm —> 


FIG 1. WIRE BASKET ASSEMBLY FOR DRAINDOWN TEST 


NOTE — The dimensions shown in the figure may vary by + 10 percent. 


IS 18104 : 2022 


4.3 Procedure 


4.3.1 For each mixture to be tested, the drain-down 
characteristics shall be determined at two temperatures, 
at the anticipated plant production temperature and at a 
temperature 10 °C higher than the anticipated 
production temperature. Duplicate samples shall be 
tested at each temperature. Therefore, a minimum of 
four samples shall be tested. 


4.3.2 Weigh the empty wire basket (W,). Place in the 
wire basket 1 200 g + 200 g of fresh, hot bitumen 
mixture sample (either prepared in the laboratory or 
from a hot mix plant) as soon aspossible without losing 
its temperature. Place the mix loosely in the basket 
without consolidating it. Determine the mass of the wire 
basket plus sample (W3). 


4.3.3 Determine the mass of the empty plate to be 
placed under the basket (W;). Hang the basket with the 
mix in the oven preheated to a selected temperature. 
Place the catch plate beneath the wire basket. Keep the 
basket in the oven for 1 h +5 min. 


4.3.4 Remove the basket and catch plate from the oven. 
Let cool to ambient temperature. Determine the mass of 
the catch plate plus the drained material (W,). 


4.3.5 Calculate the percentage of mixture which 
drained to the nearest 0.1 percent as follows: 


Drain-down (percent) = a x 100 
2 #01 
where 


W, = mass, in g, of the empty wire basket; 

W, = mass, in g, of the wire basket with sample; 

W; = mass, in g, of the empty catch plate; and 

W, = mass, in g, of the catch plate with drained 
material. 


4.3.6 Average the two drain-down results at each 
temperature and report the average to nearest 0.1 
percent 


5 METHOD B — SCHELLENBERG BINDER 
DRAINAGE TEST [FOR STONE MATRIX 
ASPHALT (SMA) MIXTURE] 


5.1 Apparatus 


5.1.1 Forced Draft Oven — Least count 1 °C and 
capable of maintaining temperatures in therange of 
120 °C to 175 °C. 


5.1.2 850 ml Glass Beaker — 98 mm diameter and 
136 mm height. 


5.1.3 Balance — least count of 0.1 g. 
5.2 Procedure 


5.2.1 Determine the mass (W,) of an empty glass beaker 
(5.1.2). Pour approximately 1 kg of the SMA mixture 
immediately into the glass beaker after mixing at the 
anticipated field mixing temperature. Re-weigh the 
beaker together with SMA (W3). 


5.2.2 Place the glass beaker with a glass or tin cover in 
an oven maintained at 170 °C + 1 °C for 1 h +1 min. 


5.2.3 At the end of Ih period, immediately remove the 
glass beaker from the oven and empty the beaker 
without any shaking or vibration. Re-weigh the beaker 
(W3). 


5.2.4 Calculate the percentage of binder drain-down 
(defined as the percentage of mass of the SMA 
deposited in the beaker) as follows: 


: WW, 
Drain-down (percent) = x 100 
WW, 


where 


W; = mass, in g, of the empty glass beaker; 

W, = mass, in g, of the beaker with SMA sample; 
and 

W; = mass, in g, of the glass beaker after draining.

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed
